title: Autonomous config reversion policy & reconciliation controller
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Goal: Implement an automated, policy-driven reversion controller that safely undoes recent config changes when certain cost, latency, or error triggers fire, and that reconciles desired vs actual state after partial failures. This is intended to reduce production incidents caused by aggressive batching/caching and automated recommendations while preserving fast rollback and auditability.

Scope:
- Define trigger conditions (cost spike %, p50/p95 latency increase, error-rate delta, rollout health checks).
- Implement guardrails that require multi-signal evidence and cool-off windows before automated reversion.
- Build a reconciliation loop that compares applied config object state in the serving fleet, the controller's intent store, and the console rollout state, and repairs drift.
- Create an operator-safe "dry-revert" simulation mode and an approvals flow for high-impact reversions.
- Emit structured events for every revert action for audit and billing reconciliation.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting batching algorithm - we only manage safe application and undo of config changes.
- Full RBAC UI (backend hooks only).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Controller can auto-revert a config change within configured policies (example policy: revert if cost > baseline by 30% AND p95 latency > 2x baseline for 5 minutes).
2) Reversion is logged as atomic, with links to original change and the selected fallback config version.
3) Reconciliation loop detects and repairs 95% of drift cases in canary/dedicated clusters within 2 minutes.
4) Dry-revert simulation produces consistent predictions matching observed revert outcome in >= 90% of test runs.
5) All revert actions surface in Console timeline and can be queried via Events API.

Design notes:
- Policy engine: use existing policy DSL from rollout service; extend with new signal predicates (cost_delta, latency_ratio, error_delta).
- Evidence aggregation: require at least two signals or a single high-confidence incident (e.g., safety_gate=true).
- Reversion strategy: prefer last-known-good variant pinned by release metadata; if absent, fallback to conservative baseline template.
- Safety nets: rate limit auto-reverts to 1 per 10m per service; add an opt-out label for customer-managed configs.
- Reconciliation: periodic compare using monotonic config version numbers + checksum; repair via orchestrated apply with backoff and conditional checks.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should the cost trigger be? (team prefers conservative defaults to avoid churn).
- Should we allow partial revert (only batching params) vs full config revert? (initial MVP: full revert).
- SLA for the controller itself — run in control-plane HA pair vs colocated operator in Dedicated clusters.

Telemetry & metrics:
- revert_attempts_total, revert_success_total, revert_failure_total, revert_latency_seconds, drift_detected_total, drift_repaired_total
- dashboard: Reverts by cause, Reverts by service, Average time to reconcile

Rollout plan:
1) Unit & integration tests + e2e dry-run in staging.
2) Canary deploy to non-critical customers with simulation mode on.
3) Enable auto-revert with conservative policy for 10 customers and monitor.
4) Gradual widening and postmortem after 2 weeks.

comments: 2026-03-01 — Kickoff: scoped MVP with PM and Design. Agreed to require 2 signals before auto-revert; Arjun to prototype evidence aggregator.
2026-03-03 — Architecture review: recommended using existing rollout policy DSL to avoid new parsing layers (feedback from Lina). Action: map cost/latency predicates into DSL nodes.

2026-03-05 — Prototype results: evidence aggregator reduces false positives in staging by ~40% compared to single-signal heuristic. Found edge case where transient GC spikes trip latency predicate; added 30s smoothing window.
2026-03-07 — PR opened: runtime/pull/1287 implements controller scaffold and policy evaluation. Needs integration tests and e2e simulation harness. Assigned to Arjun for tests.
2026-03-09 — Security review kickoff: security requested audit trail format include config hashes and operator IDs (added to acceptance criteria).

2026-03-10 — Blocker surfaced: Dedicated clusters with older agent version do not report config version stamping. Workaround: reconciliation will fallback to acceptance by checksum; follow-up ticket created ENG-75602 to upgrade agents.
